_about: Iteration 3 prompt pack (draft, revised 2026-10-25 after the identity and production reviews). Tool-agnostic: written for any modern image model. Companion to iteration-3-art-bible.md and iteration-3-assets.md; iteration-3-direction-tests.md is assembled from this file. Templates use {placeholders} filled from content/ and from 'briefs' below, by id, so new content gets prompts automatically once it has a brief.

assembly.negative_field: Pass 'negative' only to tools with a real negative-prompt field. Otherwise leave it out entirely: writing 'text, letters…' into a positive prompt tends to summon text. Describe surfaces positively instead ('plain unmarked cloth', 'blank cream pages', 'an unpainted signboard').
assembly.reference_images: Every generation in a template uses the same fixed anchor set: the locked style sheet plus 3–4 approved anchors for that template (art/reference/<template>/anchor-*.png). Never chain from the previous keeper; it compounds drift. Anything with geometry (direction tests of the courtyard, room masters, backdrops, props) also gets a structure reference (a depth or line render) captured from the engine with --capture, so the camera and light are the game's own.
assembly.seeds: Record seeds for the audit trail only. Don't rely on them for consistency: hosted models change version underneath you.
assembly.style_model: Once the anchors pass review in the engine, train one style adapter (a LoRA, or the tool's custom-model or style-reference feature) on 20–40 approved keepers of the chosen direction, and run every later batch through it. Record its file hash in the manifest. Retrain only at a review gate, never mid-batch.
assembly.transparency: Generate isolated assets on flat mid-grey (#7A7A7A), or on a background that contrasts in value with the subject. Never parchment: it's the interface's paper colour and close to a dozen pale items. Prefer the tool's native transparent output; otherwise cut with a matting model and check the edges at 2x zoom. No cast or contact shadows in the image: the engine draws them, so they stay put when a prop lifts on hover. Paint jars and flasks as glazed or opaque with the substance showing in a window; leave real see-through glass to the engine.
assembly.lettering: Hard rule: no generated lettering. Text-bearing surfaces are generated blank and the engine sets the words. Handwriting that a scene needs is drawn as unreadable flourishes.
assembly.qa: Automated gate before human review: a palette histogram against the style sheet; an alpha check (no background pixels left, no halo); a text check (OCR; any detected glyph box means reject or inpaint); a silhouette check after downscaling to the in-game size (40 px icons, 20 px spines). Then review each batch as a contact sheet at in-game size beside its anchors.

world: The Atrium: the shaded canyon floor at the very bottom of Stairfall, a city built down a cliff face in tiers of stairs, arches and lit windows. Down here the light is the cool bright sky far overhead; warmth appears only where someone has carried a light down or lit one. Things here have arrived from above and settled: books in a pile, gold in the silt, a key in a reliquary. Palette: cistern slate, verdigris, deep-pool teal, canyon moss and fall-mist grey for the shade; parchment and sandstone for paper and stone; lamp amber, ember and a little Hem-clay red as rare warm accents. Quiet and unhurried.
world_style: The painted world of the Atrium: old, used, mended things; cool blue-green shade; small warm light only from a lit source; quiet and unhurried.
negative: text, lettering, letters, words, numbers, captions, signature, watermark, logo, frame or border, cast shadow or contact shadow on isolated subjects, modern objects, plastic, rubber tubing, neon, chrome, sci-fi, photoreal human faces, the player character's body, face, hands, shadow or reflection, cozy game, chibi, kawaii, anime, storybook cottage, gore, horror, gloom, oversaturated colour, airbrushed gradients, lens flare, blurry, duplicated objects, extra limbs, gilt or gold-leaf ornament

A.name: Lamplit Ink (recommended)
A.medium: Gouache and ink, like a plate from an old naturalist's field book: observed, not whimsical. Flat opaque colour shapes with quiet visible brushwork, slightly dry edges and paper grain in the lights; a warm brown-black ink line, heavier on silhouettes and broken where light falls; two or three flat value steps per material, with coloured shadows of verdigris and slate; restrained and hand-made.

B.name: The Pop-up Stair
B.medium: A handmade paper-theatre diorama photographed in soft light: layered cut card and handmade paper, visible folds, scored edges, glue seams, cotton thread and tiny brass split pins; each depth layer a separate sheet casting a soft shadow on the one behind; matte paper colours, cool blue-green card for the shade, warm translucent tissue paper only where a lamp glows; tactile, precise, slightly imperfect.

C.name: Kiln and Glaze
C.medium: A tabletop museum model of glazed ceramic and carved, painted wood, photographed like a miniature: celadon and verdigris glazes pooling in the recesses, unglazed terracotta for clay, hand-carved wood with visible tool marks, tiny brass fittings; soft top light, shallow depth of field, warm pinpoints only where a lamp is lit; quiet, old and observed.

direction_tests.reference: Engine capture of the courtyard from its real camera (about 30° down, 31° field of view): new game, `go hub`, early evening. Paint over it, keeping its framing exactly.
direction_tests.subject: The courtyard at early evening, seen from above at the game's fixed angle. An enormous ancient tree leans about fifteen degrees out over three different pools: a wide sunlit one under the waterfall's spray, a deep dark one among the roots, a small mirror-still one ringed with flat stones that reflects the lit city above. Beside the tree a tall, lazy, pale duck-egg ribbon of waterfall drifts down the cliff. Four small houses stand around the tree: a tall, narrow grey stone house with a steep blue roof and a green door; a low timber lodge with a teal roof and a porch beside the pools; a low plaster shop with a violet roof, a chimney and a bowed window full of jars; and a round stone lodge with an ochre dome. Each has an old lamp over its door, dark and unlit. A few low iron lamp posts are just being lit. The canyon walls rise out of the top of the frame in stacked strata, stairs and warm lit windows. No people.

direction_tests.reference: The same engine capture at noon.
direction_tests.subject: The same courtyard at noon. A single long shaft of sunlight falls through the gap between the cliffs onto the widest pool and the tree's crown, turning that water pale and bright. The pool among the roots stays in green shade. Spray from the waterfall glitters in the beam. The tree's short noon shadow, about a hand's width, pools at its own roots. Small square holes in the bark at a raised hand's height are empty and dark. No people.

Inside a cramped old library in a tall, narrow stone house, looking slightly up: a long run of dark wooden bookcases along the back wall, mostly empty, with a brass lamp on the wall at the left end of the run; a reading table in front heaped with unshelved books in many worn cloth colours; a rolling ladder; dusty beams from a high window; a cup bristling with pencils and a dented biscuit tin on the table. No people.

Inside a small apothecary shop, looking slightly up: a long wooden bench with a copper mixing vessel, a heavy stone mortar and pestle, a small brass spirit burner with a blue flame, an assayer's balance and a reading glass on a stand; behind it a wall of shelves with glazed stoneware jars, string-tied, with blank paper labels; a bowed front window full of backlit jars; an empty wooden frame holding a blank sheet of paper on the wall; ash on the floorboards. No people.

A wet stone room beside a waterfall where druids keep three glass-sided tanks of pool water on a long stone ledge, looking slightly up. Each tank wears its own light: the first in warm, broken morning light and falling spray, with a branch shadow across it; the second in green, tired light filtered through tree roots, a root breaking through the wall behind it; the third glass-still and ringed with flat stones, with no ripples at all. Small bright fish, butter-yellow snails on stones, reeds with tiny glowing tips, a few slow floating sparks. Arched windows overgrown with ferns; a large clay crock, a stool and a druid's cloth bag on the wet flagstones. No people.

A round stone study at night, looking slightly up: a writing desk with an open journal of blank pages and two candles; a framed charter on the wall with a red wax seal; an old brass balance standing over a small sealed wooden reliquary; an assembly bench with tools and pinned blank sketches; a tall cedar cabinet; a chalk circle worked so neatly into the slate floor's pattern it could be decoration, glowing very faintly like a hearth after the fire is out; a round window above letting in a little moonlight. No people.

A study sheet of six small objects laid out in two rows on flat mid-grey, evenly spaced, no shadows: a pale, slender pressed leaf sealed flat under something clear and hard, its veins catching the light like threads of silver; a thumb-sized lump of gold, softly folded, as if pressed rather than found; a smooth, pale oval stone, a little translucent at the edges, cold-looking; a perfectly smooth black pearl; a heavy iron key with a plain bow and a bright silver bit; a small glazed stoneware jar of grey ash tied with string. Seen from slightly above, light from the upper left.

An open hand-bound journal on a dark wooden desk, seen from above: cloth cover re-bound along the spine, plain linen ribbon tabs down the fore-edge, deckled blank cream pages, a pencil, a red wax seal pressed in one corner, a brass lamp casting warm light across one page while the other stays cool.

style_sheet.subject: A style reference sheet laid out as tidy swatches on flat mid-grey: a row of palette chips from cool slate, verdigris, teal and moss to parchment, sandstone, amber, ember and clay red; three material swatches (wet stone with moss, worn cloth book cover, verdigris brass); one glazed jar drawn small and again large; a lamp with its warm light pool; a leaf showing the line and paint treatment. No text or labels.

hub_backdrop.subject: One layer of a painted backdrop for a canyon city, painted as one long strip that wraps around the canyon's arc (the camera orbits all the way round): {layer}. Flat, even daylight; no sky in the image; set against flat mid-grey so it can be cut out.

window_mask.source: one per city layer of anchors.backdrop_layers
window_mask.subject: A mask for the layer above: only its windows and lamps painted warm white on black, everything else black. The engine lights it at dusk and night.

room_master.reference: Capture the iteration-2 room from its camera with --capture (a preset with the room unlocked, `go <room>`, `wait 1`, `shot <room>-empty`) and use it as the structure reference.
room_master.subject: {plate} Fully furnished with: {furniture}. Seen from the room's fixed game camera: match the attached capture exactly (about 20 degrees down, 36-degree field of view). Keep interactive furniture inside the middle of the frame (from 42% to 72% across and 21% to 77% down): the left 42% sits under the working card, the right 27% under notices, the bottom 23% under the caption and satchel. No people.
room_master.notes: Method: generate the room fully furnished in one image so every prop shares perspective and light; cut each piece of furniture to its own layer and inpaint the wall behind it to make the clean plate; project iteration 2's hotspot boxes through the same camera to seed the 2D hotspot outlines and the positions of data-driven furniture, stored as data beside the plate (E2). Furniture whose count comes from content is cut once and placed by the game.

hero_turnaround.subject: A modelling reference sheet of {subject}: front, side and back views at the same scale, orthographic, flat even light, flat mid-grey background, nothing overlapping.
hero_turnaround.notes: A modelling and paint-over reference only, to the parts spec in iteration-3-assets.md. If an image-to-3D tool is tried, its output is a blockout to retopologise, never the shipped mesh.

ui_piece.subject: {piece}: a real object from the Keeper's desk, on flat dark slate (#2F3B44), straight-on and evenly lit, no shadow; blank of any text or symbol unless described.

key_art.subject: The courtyard at dusk seen from low by the largest pool, looking up past the great leaning tree and the lazy pale waterfall to the tiers of the city lighting their windows. The four small houses stand around the tree, each with an old dark lamp over its door; the courtyard is lit only by a few low iron lamp posts. A satchel rests on the pool's edge with a pale pressed leaf just peeking out. The upper third is left calm for the title. No people.

backdrop_layers.layer: the highest, farthest layer: the snowy mountain shrines of the High Hallows and the top of the Long Stair, tiny and pale

the upper tiers: the grand, slightly forgetful Crown with its charter office, and below it the Gallery's markets and glassworks; at one side three great sluices of oak and iron, water pouring through the two nearest the cliff while the outermost stands shut and dry, moss on its gate; each tier's small, old waystation tree, joined by the zigzag of the Long Stair

the nearest cliff edges framing the canyon: stair landings, rope bridges, and pilgrim cords and lanterns hanging down into view

courtyard_scene._note: Designer brief, 2026-10-25: use Higgsfield to make the courtyard scene (the tall tree, the four distinct houses and the pools) so it feels like a natural corner of a large medieval city. Higgsfield's 3D models lift one image of an object into a mesh; none generates a whole scene. So it's two steps: a look-development keyframe, then the courtyard painted as a miniature diorama (an object) and lifted to 3D. Prices aren't published through the API, so check the balance after each generation.

keyframe.reference: Optional: the engine capture hub-evening.png (camera and layout only).
keyframe.subject: The Atrium: a quiet courtyard at the very bottom of a large medieval city built down the side of a canyon, seen from above at a thirty-degree angle. At its centre an enormous ancient tree leans about fifteen degrees out over three different pools: a wide one under the spray of a tall, lazy, pale waterfall drifting down the cliff; a deep, dark one among the roots; a small, mirror-still one ringed with flat stones. Four small houses stand around the tree, each unmistakable by its silhouette: a tall, narrow grey stone house with a steep blue slate roof and a green door; a long, low timber lodge with a teal reed-thatch roof and a deep porch beside the pools; a low plaster shop with a violet tiled roof, a brick chimney and a bowed window full of jars; and a round stone lodge with an ochre dome and a small spire. The courtyard is no island: the city crowds its edges and climbs the cliff behind it in tier on tier of timber-framed and stone houses, with stairs zigzagging down, arched passages, little bridges, chimneys, washing lines and warm lit windows. Mossy paving, worn steps, a few iron lamp posts; the old lamps over the four doors are dark. Early evening: the courtyard in cool shade, the high city still catching the last warm light. No people.

diorama.reference: The approved keyframe, as a style and layout reference.
diorama.subject: A detailed miniature diorama of a medieval courtyard, built on a thick square base of layered stone and earth, shown whole and centred on a plain flat mid-grey background, from a three-quarter angle above, evenly lit with soft light and no cast shadows. On the base: an enormous ancient tree leaning out over three small pools; a lazy waterfall pouring down a stepped cliff in the back corner into the largest pool; four small, distinct houses around the tree (a tall narrow stone house with a steep blue roof and a green door; a low timber lodge with a teal thatched roof and a porch; a low plaster shop with a violet roof, a chimney and a bowed window; a round stone lodge with an ochre dome). Along the two back edges, the start of a large medieval city: tall stacked timber-framed and stone houses climbing the cliff, with stairs and arches, cut off cleanly at the edge of the base. Chunky, readable, solid forms; nothing floating; nothing cropped by the frame.
diorama.medium: A hand-painted miniature: matte gouache-painted surfaces with soft brushwork, warm brown-black painted linework along edges, flat colour shapes, coloured shadows of verdigris and slate.

lift.why: Tripo P2 removes baked-in lighting before texturing (the bible wants unlit albedo, because the cel shader does the light) and caps faces at 50,000, safely under raylib's 65,535-vertex limit per part. PBR maps aren't used by the cel shader.
lift.caveat: A look test, not a shipping asset. One fused mesh can't light its windows, close shutters or sway the canopy apart from the trunk, and the engine can't draw it in the cel style until task E1 lands (iteration-3-art-bible.md, How the art meets the engine).

story_vignettes.scene: evening on a long stone stair: a small wax-sealed note passed from hand to hand down the tiers of the city, from one lit doorway to the next, toward a dark courtyard far below; only townsfolk's hands and sleeves are seen.

a slate floor at night: a closed chalk circle worked so neatly into the floor's pattern it could be decoration, glowing faintly the way a hearth glows after the fire is out; its centre empty (the engine composites the player's own remnant).

close on the bark of a great tree at a raised hand's height: a column of empty square nail-holes ringed with smooth dark bark; a ladder leaning on the trunk with a notebook on its top rung, one gold-wrapped nail lying on the notebook; afternoon light.
candlelight on an old brass balance standing over a sealed wooden reliquary; a torn scrap of old paper covered in faded, unreadable handwriting lies beside a black pearl in a dish.
a brass balance level at last over an open cedar reliquary lined with worn velvet, a long empty hollow pressed into the velvet, dust turning in the candlelight.

night in the courtyard with the four old lamps over the four doors lit for the first time in eighty years; small figures on the last stairs from the tier above, looking down; warm light on the pools; a jar of glowing air waiting on flat stones by the water. The great tree is exactly as always.

a library table covered by an unrolled map of waterworks and sluices (drawn shapes, no writing), its corners weighted with teacups; an old book open beside it; a pinch of silver silt in a twist of paper.

two old pages side by side under a honeyed lantern, both covered in the same small handwriting drawn as unreadable flourishes, in identical ink; a pale pressed leaf under clear wax and a heavy iron key with a silver bit rest nearby.

a warm evening picnic under the great leaning tree, seen from the Keeper's own place on the blanket: a good teacup set down in the foreground, far too much food, a goldfish in a jar of water, lamps lit around the pools; the others seen from behind or far off, no faces.
a long run of bookcases full and in perfect order, the lamp at the end of the run glowing, a single fingertip trail in the dust along the spines; quiet.
a bowed shop window seen from inside in morning sun: a hand-drawn map of connected circles (no writing) pinned to the glass, sunlight shining through it onto jars and the floor.
the edge of a sunlit pool: a crowd of small bright fish turning circles, butter-yellow snails on the stones, a druid's wet boots at the water's edge.

trailer_capture._note: Shot in the engine with --capture and a scripted camera, not generated: a video model would morph Old Stoic and show things the game can't do. Generated video is for internal mood boards only.

shots.shot: A slow orbit over the courtyard from noon into dusk as the city's windows come on.
A book slides into its gap and the shelf glows; dust drifts in the window beam.
Elements drop into the copper vessel; it swirls; a new jar pops onto the shelf.
Food flakes drift down from above the frame into a tank; small fish turn circles; a hatchling pops.
A chalk circle in the slate floor brightens slowly, like a banked hearth, while dust turns in the candlelight. Nothing is shown being remade.
Night falls over the courtyard; the lamp posts come on, then the city above becomes a wall of warm windows.
